[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38888018-United-Critics/] Please follow [b]United Critics[/b] for quality reviews[/url] [h1]Story[/h1] The story is pretty simple so I will just copy it from the game description. Without fear, you signed the contract which would forever sever your ties to the world above, and now it is your sworn duty to brave the abyss and uncover the secrets of the old world. Your death is guaranteed, but so is your status as a legend. That is basically it. [h1]Gameplay[/h1] The gameplay is a mix of fun and methodical combat and tactics. The most important things that will decide if you win is understanding the pathfinding of enemies and also how both of your attacks work. You will have to not only kill hordes of enemies but also destroy their spawn points and find keys to be able to unlock parts of the level and get to exit. It is really important to learn enemies move speed and for the ones that shoot at you their bullets color and attack patterns. You go deeper and deeper underground and defeat more powerful monsters on each level till you will find the last level with dragon that is the boss in hopes of finding the answers to your questions about the old world. Along the way you will also meet some unique enemies that have their own attack patterns and are basically mini-bosses. With time you also become more powerful thanks to collecting XP from defeated enemies and leveling your attacks and stats. There are 21 heroes to choose from – 4 are unlocked from the start – the rest you have to unlock by using the gold that you can find on the levels. Gold is also used for unlocking the permanent upgrades so all your next runs will become little easier. Levels are good as they are a mix of premade maps that the game picks randomly from the map pool and then it randomizes where the keys and potions and chests will be and what types of enemies will be in what part of each level and where the exit will be placed. The game also requires you to move fast as on each level after you spend 7 minutes there the death will spawn and will start to move slowly in your direction trying to kill you. For me this is not a big problem as the more you learn about the game and your heroes the easier it is to clean each level before the death spawn or even just pick the last chest or kill a few enemies when it spawn and escape before it gets near you. But for some players such mechanic that limits the time they can spend on each level can be something that they can’t deal with and thus this game might not be fun for them. I think that some heroes are just more powerful than others just because they got better attacks in my opinion by having better attack patterns and speed etc. I think it is mostly personal feeling but I just find that the heroes with attacks that have the best speed are the strongest while heroes with the slowest attacks are the weakest. I think this is because of how fast spawners can create new monsters thus making fast attacks more valuable than slow ones. [h1]Graphic and sound[/h1] The game uses a good looking pixel sprites so all the heroes you can pick and all the enemies you will fight against look good. All heroes attacks also looks good and are unique for each hero thus showing the amount of work that was put into pixel graphics to represents these attacks and each hero own identity. I also like that each level has it’s own music setting the tone for each level. Because each level has it’s own music the music in the game is never boring – it would be hard to listen to the same music for one hour but it is not boring if every 4-8 minutes you get to a new level and you get new music that fits that level perfectly. [h1]Conclusion[/h1] If you like to descend deeper into a dungeon and slaughter more powerful enemies each time this game is for you. Overall score 7/10

As someone who loved the original Gauntlet and very much enjoys Vampire Survivors, I really expected to at least like this. But surprisingly I didn't, and the reasons why are easy to explain. But first of all, is my review even valid? After all, I only have 1 hour in the game. Well if you're me, you'll probably say "no" because most games these days simply can't be reviewed in an hour. But this is the first game in recent memory that was so absolutely boring within the first hour, that I just couldn't play any more. Note that I only played single player. Here's why I didn't enjoy this game: 1. There is no enemy variation. There are 3 basic enemies: guy that takes 3 shots to kill, guy that takes 2 shots but is fast, and guy that takes 3 shots but shoots projectiles at you. There are very minor variations, like some projectiles which can be shot and those that can't, but that's the vast majority of enemy complexity. In addition to the basic enemies, there is an occasional elite enemy that has many more hit points and shoots several projectiles in a blast with a varying pattern. New levels don't introduce new enemies. You fight this same score of enemies at least all the way from levels 1 through (I believe) 6. The only thing that changes is their stats increase and their sprite changes. 2. Upgrades are meaningless. As you increase your stats, you power through the levels, at which point the monsters all have higher stats. This means that with like even 7 upgrades to your main weapon (a shiny, golden upgrade), you're still fighting enemies that take 2 or 3 shots to kill. Eventually, at the end of an upgrade line you can specialize your weapon, but this specialization is a sidegrade, not a more effective upgrade. At least this is true of the 2 characters that I played to that point. I'm just not willing to play another hour to find out for two more. 3. Every level is the same. There are 2 main elements to a level: keys for locked walls, and shootable walls. You walk through the maze, looking for a copper, silver and gold key, in that order. Once you have the gold key, you find the exit and leave. Sometimes you might find an exit where you don't need all 3 keys. Here's the thing: if any one of these things above were not an issue, I think I would have fun with this game. It can be okay for the levels to be repetitive if the enemies aren't, or vice-versa. In this game there's just enough similarity that I never felt as though I was making any kind of choice. Most survival games have quite boring enemies, but the upgrades significantly impact survivability and gameplay. There are many classes, and the one special class that I unlocked was the elf. The elf has a homing primary weapon and a primeable secondary weapon. It sounds fun on paper, but because there is so little enemy, level or upgrade variation, it doesn't matter that the class was designed this way. The game felt too similarly to the other two classes I played. Maybe these issues are alleviated after 25 minutes into a run, but having to play through such a 25 minutes every time is just not something I'm eager to do. As a Gauntlet fan, I want to make a final note that I haven't seen another reviewer mention. There are a lot of mechanics from Gauntlet that this game does not adapt, but the one most worth mentioning is that the levels are randomly generated, and relatively small. For anyone who remembers, especially Gauntlet II on NES, the original game had great level design. Sadly, while these levels are serviceable, no individual level stands out or enhances the gameplay experience.

The dev has gone on record that the old arcade Gauntlet games were the main inspiration for this--especially given that the Arrowhead Gauntlet game doesn't play like the old arcade Gauntlet games--but calling it "roguelike Gauntlet" doesn't quite seem accurate. It [i]is[/i] a fun little game in its own right, though; the price is just right for a game as simple as this one. Rather than effectively an endless score attack as the original inspiration was, this game is a roguelike which has you progress through 10 maps selected from a pool, followed by a final boss level, then (should you survive all of the above) a Vampire Survivors-esque infinite horde until you finally croak. This is much, [i]much[/i] easier than OG Gauntlet; instead of having a set amount of health constantly ticking down, you have a set 100 health that takes damage when you get hit. Health is refilled in between floors and will also regenerate on each floor, albeit very slowly. Every level has you find three different flavors of keys to unlock doors to murder the enemies inside, the things that spawn said enemies, and grab treasure. There [i]is[/i] a timer that isn't tied to your health. Instead, you have a 6-7 minute time limit on each floor before a grim reaper is summoned. He can be kited around because he is [i]very[/i] slow, but given that he goes through walls and fires projectiles, it's one more thing to keep track of if you don't bail out in time. The microprogression is that as you go through the dungeons and kill things, you get experience points for levels and get a chance from three stat increases at random (attack power, defense, life regen, mana regen, walk speed, attack speed, crit chance). If you die, it's back to the title screen. The macroprogression is that you keep gold in between runs to spend on upgrades. Some are basic (attack buffs, defense buffs), while some are more exciting (reroll your level up choices, better chances to find treasure rooms in between levels, curses that make the game harder). I like it enough, especially for a game that costs as much as a cup of coffee, but that comes with stipulations. [h2] The Good [/h2] [list] [*]It's certainly more accessible compared to OG Gauntlet. [*]Having more than one shot on the screen compared to OG Gauntlet feels nice. [*]There are lots of bullets, but the hitboxes are fair and I rarely feel like I've taken a cheap shot. [*]Lots of character options to unlock that go beyond the basic "fighter/thief/wizard" archetypes, so you'll probably find something you like if you unlock enough characters. If you wanted to play Gauntlet as a wolfman with a pump-action shotgun and grenades to pretend you're Brad Fang, you can do that. [*]Each run is bite-sized as roguelikes go; a start-to-finish playthrough usually takes about an hour. [*]The music is great, and [i]will[/i] get stuck in your head. Shoutout to the mummy/scorpion stage tune. [*]There is a lot to unlock here for the number-goes-up enthusiasts. [/list] [h2] The Bad [/h2] [list] [*]As of right now, It's too easy. I expect a game both based off Rogue and Gauntlet to ruthlessly murder me, but truth is, I have yet to actually [i]die[/i] in the main campaign on the few runs I've been doing (all with different characters). The mob A.I. is simple and very easy to break as a result, and unlike Gauntlet, the projectiles in this game are slow and the enemies have actual chill in that they don't instantly blast you the second you enter their line of sight. [*]The rank 10 weapon mods mostly suck. Some can be fun but almost all of them come with massive penalties that make them either stupidly unwieldy or in some cases just flat-out worse than the default options. [*]The stat increases on each run don't really hide the fact that most of the time you're only increasing your stats to keep even with the enemies' increasing stats. [*]Similarly, most of the macroprogression stat increases are just kind of there. The main reason most of them exist is to justify bringing them to Curse runs, which will otherwise be an absolute slog with how spongy the enemies get. [/list] [h2] The Weird [/h2] Character balance is all over the place. I understand that when you have not-quite-30 characters not everything is going to be perfect, but some of these feel like they weren't tested compared to others, and I haven't even unlocked the endgame one that costs 100000 gold. In general, characters tend to fall on a spectrum of being better at mobs vs. better at elites/bossing, and as the game is 99.9% mobs, you can guess who's usually better because it's not like they're incapable of beating boss fights. On the end of ones I'm [i]not[/i] impressed with, the Paladin is slow to fire, short ranged, and hits hard but not hard enough to make enough of a difference on breakpoints/TTK compared to other characters. His alt-fire is also short-ranged and not that impressive for a get-off-me technique, especially because [i]it has a blind spot at point-blank range[/i] which kinda misses the point of a get-off-me move. One of his upgrades makes your primary throwing weapon hit much harder, but also gives it a firing delay so long you can barely keep up with spawners unless you spend the entire remainder of the game rerolling dexterity. Now that I mention it, the game has a lot of what I can only call "slow-roll" characters; that is, they start with attacks that hit hard but fire extremely slowly compared to others, and these tend to be a [i]total[/i] slog to play with until you've hit about midway through the game and gotten actual stat boosts because you can actually kill things in a timely manner. Not [i]difficult[/i], mind you, but a slog. They make the already kinda-tedious first levels even more tedious with their long attack cooldowns. Maybe fewer of these would've been nice, but it is what it is; unless you're achievement hunting I guess you have other choices, like the starter Thief, who is very fun and much more APM-heavy. Speaking of other faster characters... Contrast the above with, the Merchant--who I initially figured would be a joke character, as merchants usually are--is like playing a Gauntlet elf who has short attack range but [i]permanent piercing and reflective shots[/i] that you have multiple of on the screen at a time. His coins can bounce three times off of walls, and rebounding shots can connect on the same enemy. His alt-fire is a shotgun blast of coins that is not as impressive in big open areas but might as well be a "♥♥♥♥ off, I win" attack in the crowded hallways that normally make up this game. The A.I. doesn't have an answer for a railgun that can bounce around corners. He might have slightly more trouble with the final boss than certain other characters because he has absolutely no means of taking advantage of wallbounces, but that's not enough to make up for how much he walks over the rest of the game. All said and done, though, it's fun. Looking forward to what the dev works on in the future.

I thought it looked kind of fun but it actually feels very slow and repetitive. Enemies aren't really interesting, the classes feel very very similar and the grind is really long. I rushed the +200% gold curse upgrade and still it felt like it was taking ages to buy anything. I wanted to see the rest of the characters and see the end but it's just not fun enough to actually play. You do the same thing every floor no matter what character you picked.

Hard and fun!

Maybe if you're a hardcore Gauntlet fan, then maybe this will fly for you.. I just found that it felt like there weren't any meaningful powerups to give me that "one more run" feeling.. I liked it enough to play what I've played, but after that things seemed to just be the same so I stopped. beef up the level up choices and maybe it'll help.

Maybe this game was meant for a very specific and niche audience but if you like modern roguelikes/bullet hells similar to vampire survivors then you might not like this. I should preface this by saying that I never played the original Gauntlet so I don't know what that was like. This game feels slow and lacks variety. The upgrades every time you level up, feel inconsequential. They are things like "+2% attack speed" or damage or defense, etc. They're very slight number upgrades so not particularly fun to choose between. You never really feel powerful or unique. It's not like The Binding of Isaac where, by the end of the run, you're an abomination but you do something cool. The pixel art is very charming though and the level design is simple but functional. Didn't really play with music on so I don't have an opinion on that. Game just wasn't for me.
awesome addictive game

Full playthrough: https://youtu.be/6K-E_LrvFgk?si=k2O6eimiuyaF0578 So I originally gave this game a bad review because some of the mechanics of the game just really pissed me off. The leveling almost feels pointless because half the time you're only given just 1 stat, and 1 stat doesnt do anything. So many tiny little corridors that are hard to dodge and I feel like the leveling of the attacks-- when they get to level 10-- they just feel arbitrary and hardly thought out: You got Faster attack, Bigger attack and 2+ attacks. Its rarely any different from this. But I couldn't stop playing it! The music in this game I think is what sells it the most. The music in this game is absolutely gorgeous and so well made. Whoever made it needs an Oscar, and Oscars arent even for music. The gameplay loop is also just addicting. Im a huge fan of the Gauntlet series and thats what this game is; a loveletter to Gauntlet. I just hope this game keeps getting more GOOD updates to keep me coming back. Unfortunately the most recent update kinda sucked... adding in all these arbitary updates like More Gold/More Enemies, Manaburst, etc. Unless im missing something they're all awful. Just give me Damage or Spirit.
I would say NO, It kinda looks cool and retro, even really fun, but when you spend some hours (for me at least) you can see it´s no more than that, progression its just useless.

I wanted to like this game but it is just too much of a grind to feel any real progress, and yea yea I get it, there are upgrades you can BUY after you have been grinding to make it slightly better but you lost me at this point. Not worth my time to grind for a game of this type and depth. Others have said the same thing, too slow and very dull game design. It was like someone said "Hey why not make a Gauntlet clone and add progression but remove as much joy as possible from the original arcade experience." I get it, this is not the Gauntlet of the arcade, did not expect it, but I did not expect dull, slow and unexciting mechanics cluttering the game to be worth it. Too many other games out there to slog through one that does not encourage you to play more.
This game is similar to gauntlet from the arcades back in the day. So if you enjoyed that style of game you should like this one.
